summary: A 1941 steel lookout tower, 30.5 m, in Albert County; a 1963 report calls it abandoned and moves its living quarters. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: Galvanized steel tower with an octagonal, glass-enclosed observer's cabin
facts.status_note: Last described as abandoned in a 1963 government report. No source found describes the site today.
facts.agency: New Brunswick Department of Lands and Mines

events.note: Canada Lookouts dates the build to 1941 and cites the 105th annual report of the Department of Lands and Mines.
The report for the year ending 31 March 1964 (filed under 1963 on the page) calls the tower abandoned. The closing date is not given.
Living quarters moved to New Ireland Road for game protection. The page does not say what happened to the tower itself.

evidence.supports: Built 1941: new 100 ft galvanized steel lookout tower, octagonal glass-enclosed observer's cabin, telephone lines, observer's living quarters
evidence.quote: 1941: "A new 100 foot galvanized steel Lookout Tower with octagonal glass enclosed observer's cabin, connecting telephone lines and observer's living quarters was built with the cooperation of the Licenses and timber land owners operating in the district.

evidence.supports: Site: about 1.5 miles north of Teahan Corner, Albert County
evidence.quote: This was erected at Doyle Hill about one and a half miles north of Teahan Corner in Albert County.

evidence.supports: 1963 report: the tower is the abandoned Lookout Tower at Doyle Hill; living quarters moved to New Ireland Road for game protection
evidence.quote: Living quarters at the abandoned Lookout Tower at Doyle Hill was moved to New Ireland Road for Game Protection.

evidence.supports: Source for the 1963 entry: the 127th report, covering the year ending 31 March 1964

notes_for_editor: Single secondary source: the Canada's Fire Lookouts page quotes the New Brunswick Department of Lands and Mines annual reports (105th for 1941; 127th, year ending 31 March 1964, filed by the page under 1963). The reports themselves were not read. The 1941 and 1963 years are the page's own labels. Two searches found nothing on what stands today or whether the site is public. Unfetched lead: a Provincial Archives of New Brunswick catalogue item, 'A circular map centered on the Doyle Hill fire tower', refers to a 1960 list of NB fire towers (P211/10229); it may hold more on the tower's fate.
